+import requests
+from requests.models import PreparedRequest
+
+def test_trim_leading_slashes():
+    # Test case 1: multiple leading slashes in path
+    url = 'http://example.com///foo'
+    req = requests.Request('GET', url)
+    prep = req.prepare()
+    print(f"URL: {url} -> {prep.url}")
+    assert prep.url == 'http://example.com/foo', f"Expected http://example.com/foo, got {prep.url}"
+
+    # Test case 2: path is just multiple slashes
+    url = 'http://example.com////'
+    req = requests.Request('GET', url)
+    prep = req.prepare()
+    print(f"URL: {url} -> {prep.url}")
+    assert prep.url == 'http://example.com/', f"Expected http://example.com/, got {prep.url}"
+
+    # Test case 3: single leading slash (should be preserved)
+    url = 'http://example.com/foo'
+    req = requests.Request('GET', url)
+    prep = req.prepare()
+    print(f"URL: {url} -> {prep.url}")
+    assert prep.url == 'http://example.com/foo', f"Expected http://example.com/foo, got {prep.url}"
+
+    # Test case 4: no path (should result in /)
+    url = 'http://example.com'
+    req = requests.Request('GET', url)
+    prep = req.prepare()
+    print(f"URL: {url} -> {prep.url}")
+    assert prep.url == 'http://example.com/', f"Expected http://example.com/, got {prep.url}"
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    try:
+        test_trim_leading_slashes()
+        print("All tests passed!")
+    except AssertionError as e:
+        print(f"Test failed: {e}")
+        exit(1)
